# QS-PROC-02 Quench and temper process window (P1)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-IH02

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptable process window and associated controls for quench and temper operations for billets fed from Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 at Plant P1, line P1-L2. It applies to all billets processed using EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and is used to set control limits, inspection criteria, and records retention for downstream ring rolling and heat treat operations. This document supplements operating procedures listed in the Related Documents section and is intended for production, quality, and maintenance staff responsible for process control and conformance.

Requirements table
| Parameter | Requirement | Rationale | Reference procedure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Induction billet heater setpoint for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 | The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C. | Establishes metallurgical starting condition for quench and temper to achieve required microstructure and hardness after ring rolling. | SOP-P1-L2-01 |
| Billet tracking and identification | All billets entering the quench and temper line shall retain unique heat and lot identity through processing and inspection records. | Traceability for nonconforming material and root cause analysis. | SOP-P1-L2-03 |
| Process parameter recording | Heater setpoint, measured billet temperature at transfer point, and operator confirmation shall be recorded for every production run. | Demonstrates control of the thermal process and provides data for trend analysis. | SOP-P1-L2-01 |
| Calibration and equipment verification | Temperature measurement devices and EQ-P1-L2-IH02 control sensors shall be verified per calibration plan and documented. | Ensures measurement accuracy for compliance to the target billet temperature. | SOP-P1-L2-05 |
| Hold and release criteria | Billets not meeting identification or recording requirements shall be segregated and held from production release until disposition. | Prevents use of unverified material and protects final product quality. | SOP-P1-L2-03 |

Inspection method
Background and rationale
The target billet temperature is set to provide a repeatable starting condition for quench and temper that aligns with alloy heat treat response and the expectations of downstream ring rolling. Measured billet temperature at the transfer point provides the most representative value for the mass entering the quench medium; therefore, control and inspection focus on the transfer point reading and the documentation of heater control output. Records serve both immediate inspection and longer term process capability assessment.

Procedure
- Verify that EQ-P1-L2-IH02 control displays the setpoint described in this document prior to starting a run per SOP-P1-L2-01.
- Measure billet temperature at the transfer point using the facility approved pyrometer or thermocouple method referenced in SOP-P1-L2-01. Record the measured value in the process log with the billet heat/lot identification from SOP-P1-L2-03.
- For each production run, confirm that calibration status for temperature sensors used on EQ-P1-L2-IH02 is current and documented per SOP-P1-L2-05. Attach calibration evidence to the run packet.
- When inspecting billets, record visual condition notes and any deviations from expected surface appearance. Note any indications that could affect quench performance and include these observations in the run log.

Examples
- Example inspection entries should include the billet heat/lot id, the measured transfer point temperature, the operator initials, and a link to the EQ-P1-L2-IH02 control log. Use the forms prescribed in SOP-P1-L2-03.
- If multiple billets are processed in a single heater cycle, record a representative transfer point temperature for the cycle and list the billet identifiers covered by that cycle in the run log.

Records to keep
- Process run log with heater setpoint confirmation, transfer point temperature readings, billet heat/lot identifiers, and operator confirmation; retain with production records per SOP-P1-L2-03.
- Calibration certificates and verification records for temperature measurement devices used with EQ-P1-L2-IH02; file per SOP-P1-L2-05.
- Disposition records for any segregated or reworked billets, including nonconformance reports and corrective action documentation.

Nonconformance handling
Detection and initial containment
- Any billet or run that lacks the required identification, measurement, or documentation shall be segregated and held. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-03 for segregation tagging and immediate containment measures.
Investigation and disposition
- Conduct investigation to determine root cause using process records, EQ-P1-L2-IH02 control logs, calibration records, and operator interviews. Document findings in the run packet.
- Disposition options include reheat under controlled conditions, rework per applicable procedures, or scrap. The disposition must be approved by quality and production leads and recorded with the billet heat/lot id.
Corrective action and prevention
- Implement corrective actions based on root cause. Actions may include adjustments to SOP steps, retraining of operators, or equipment maintenance on EQ-P1-L2-IH02. Record corrective actions and their verification.
- Review related process controls and update references to SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-03, and SOP-P1-L2-05 as required to prevent recurrence.

Related documents
- SOP-P1-L2-01
- SOP-P1-L2-03
- SOP-P1-L2-05

Revision control
Maintain this document and associated records in the document control system. Changes to the target or procedural controls require approval through the formal revision process.
